claim: Log group data is always encrypted in CloudWatch Logs; by default CloudWatch Logs uses server-side encryption with 256-bit AES-GCM to encrypt log data at rest, and as an alternative you can use AWS KMS.
question: Is CloudWatch Logs data encrypted at rest by default, and can you use your own KMS key?

values.display: you can use AWS Key Management Service

evidence.quote: Log group data is always encrypted in CloudWatch Logs. By default, CloudWatch Logs uses server-side encryption with 256-bit Advanced Encryption Standard Galois/Counter Mode (AES-GCM) to encrypt log data at rest. As an alternative, you can use AWS Key Management Service for this encryption.

claim: Encryption with AWS KMS is enabled at the log group level, by associating a KMS key with a log group either when you create the log group or after it exists.
question: At what level do you apply a customer managed KMS key in CloudWatch Logs?

values.display: enabled at the log group level

evidence.quote: Encryption using AWS KMS is enabled at the log group level, by associating a KMS key with a log group, either when you create the log group or after it exists.

claim: After you associate a KMS key with a log group, all newly ingested data for the log group is encrypted using this key and stored encrypted for its retention period; CloudWatch Logs must have permissions for the KMS key whenever encrypted data is requested.
question: What does associating a KMS key with a log group encrypt, and what does CloudWatch Logs need?

values.display: must have permissions for the KMS key

evidence.quote: After you associate a KMS key with a log group, all newly ingested data for the log group is encrypted using this key. This data is stored in encrypted format throughout its retention period. CloudWatch Logs decrypts this data whenever it is requested. CloudWatch Logs must have permissions for the KMS key whenever encrypted data is requested.

claim: If you disassociate a KMS key from a log group, CloudWatch Logs encrypts newly ingested data with its default encryption method, and data ingested earlier stays encrypted with the KMS key.
question: What happens to existing log data when you disassociate a KMS key from a log group?

values.display: remains encrypted with the KMS key

evidence.quote: If you later disassociate a KMS key from a log group, CloudWatch Logs encrypts newly ingested data using the CloudWatch Logs default encryption method. All previously ingested data that was encrypted with the KMS key remains encrypted with the KMS key.

claim: If a KMS key that encrypted log data is disabled, CloudWatch Logs is unable to read the logs that were encrypted with that key.
question: What happens to encrypted logs if the KMS key is disabled?

qualifiers.condition: Applies to logs encrypted with that key, including after the key was disassociated from the log group.

evidence.quote: However, if the key is later disabled, then CloudWatch Logs is unable to read the logs that were encrypted with that key.

claim: If you revoke CloudWatch Logs access to an associated KMS key or delete the key, your encrypted data in CloudWatch Logs can no longer be retrieved.
question: What happens to log data if you delete the KMS key or revoke CloudWatch Logs access to it?

evidence.quote: If you revoke CloudWatch Logs access to an associated key or delete an associated KMS key, your encrypted data in CloudWatch Logs can no longer be retrieved.

claim: CloudWatch Logs supports only symmetric KMS keys; do not use an asymmetric key to encrypt log group data.
question: Can an asymmetric KMS key encrypt a CloudWatch Logs log group?

values.display: Do not use an asymmetric key

evidence.quote: CloudWatch Logs supports only symmetric KMS keys. Do not use an asymmetric key to encrypt the data in your log groups.

claim: You cannot associate a KMS key with an existing log group using the CloudWatch console.
question: Can you add a KMS key to an existing log group in the console?

evidence.quote: You can't associate a KMS key with an existing log group using the CloudWatch console.

claim: When you create a data protection policy, sensitive data that matches the selected data identifiers is masked by default at all egress points, including CloudWatch Logs Insights, metric filters and subscription filters, and only users with the logs:Unmask IAM permission can view unmasked data.
question: Who can see unmasked sensitive data in CloudWatch Logs with a data protection policy?

evidence.quote: When you create a data protection policy, then by default, sensitive data that matches the data identifiers you've selected is masked at all egress points, including CloudWatch Logs Insights, metric filters, and subscription filters. Only users who have the `logs:Unmask` IAM permission can view unmasked data.

claim: You can create a data protection policy for all log groups in your account or for individual log groups; an account-wide policy applies to both existing log groups and log groups created in the future.
question: Does an account-level data protection policy cover log groups created later?

values.display: log groups that are created in the future
for all log groups in your account

evidence.quote: You can create a data protection policy for all log groups in your account, and you can also create a data protection policies for individual log groups. When you create a policy for your entire account, it applies to both existing log groups and log groups that are created in the future.

claim: Sensitive data is detected and masked when it is ingested into the log group, so log events ingested before you set a data protection policy are not masked.
question: Does a new data protection policy mask log events that were ingested earlier?

values.display: when it is ingested into the log group

evidence.quote: Sensitive data is detected and masked when it is ingested into the log group. When you set a data protection policy, log events ingested to the log group before that time are not masked.

claim: Each log group can have only one log group-level data protection policy, but that policy can specify many managed data identifiers; if you also have an account-wide policy, both policies apply to the log group.
question: How many data protection policies can one log group have?

values.display: only one log group-level data protection policy
both policies apply to that log group

evidence.quote: Each log group can have only one log group-level data protection policy, but that policy can specify many managed data identifiers to audit and mask.
If you create a data protection policy for your entire account and you also create a policy for a single log group, both policies apply to that log group.

claim: CloudWatch Logs data protection offers managed data identifiers, preconfigured data types you can select to protect financial data, personal health information (PHI) and personally identifiable information (PII).
question: Which kinds of sensitive data can CloudWatch Logs data protection detect?

evidence.quote: CloudWatch Logs supports many *managed data identifiers*, which offer preconfigured data types you can select to protect financial data, personal health information (PHI), and personally identifiable information (PII).

claim: Masking sensitive data is supported for log groups in both the Standard and Infrequent Access log classes.
question: Does data protection masking work on Infrequent Access log groups?

values.display: both the Standard and Infrequent Access log classes

evidence.quote: Masking sensitive data is supported for log groups in both the Standard and Infrequent Access log classes.

claim: Deletion protection prevents accidental deletion of log groups and their log streams: when enabled on a log group it blocks all deletion operations until explicitly disabled, and by default it is not enabled.
question: Is deletion protection on by default for CloudWatch log groups?

values.display: By default, deletion protection is not enabled

evidence.quote: Deletion protection is a safeguard that prevents accidental deletion of log groups and their log streams. When enabled on a log group, deletion protection blocks all deletion operations until it is explicitly disabled. By default, deletion protection is not enabled.

claim: You can enable deletion protection when you create a new log group or on existing log groups.
question: Can you turn on deletion protection for a log group that already exists?

evidence.quote: You can enable deletion protection when creating a new log group or on existing log groups.
